title: [Bugfix][KV Connector] Restore state after KV load rejection
body:
## Purpose

Fixes #49250.

When a synchronous external KV load is rejected under
`kv_load_failure_policy="recompute"`, scheduler state is rewound but Model
Runner V2 can retain the old device-side computed-token offset. With
overlapping batches, output already in flight can also mutate reset scheduler
state or be delivered after the request has been rescheduled. The result does
not match full recomputation.

This change:

- marks the exact in-flight token positions stale and clears speculative and
  placeholder state when a failed load is recomputed;
- propagates an explicit `rewound_req_ids` marker with cached-request data;
- applies the scheduler's absolute computed-token offset to Model Runner V2's
  device-side request state only for those explicit rollbacks; and
- adds focused scheduler and worker regression tests, including a multi-token
  speculative async frame.

There is no connector-specific special case.

This is materially different from #49252. That PR's scheduler fix derives a
frame count from `num_output_placeholders - 1` and explicitly scopes out
speculative decoding and diffusion. This change uses the existing exact
`num_in_flight_tokens` accounting and an explicit CPU-to-GPU rewind signal; it
was validated with EAGLE3. The difference was documented on #49250 before this
draft was opened.

## Test Plan

```bash
python -m pytest -q \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_kv_load_failure_recovery.py \
  tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_model_runner_v2.py

ruff check \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_kv_load_failure_recovery.py \
  tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_model_runner_v2.py \
  vllm/v1/core/sched/output.py \
  vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py \
  vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_runner.py

ruff format --check \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_kv_load_failure_recovery.py \
  tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_model_runner_v2.py \
  vllm/v1/core/sched/output.py \
  vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py \
  vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_runner.py

git diff --check origin/main...HEAD
```

GPU negative-control protocol:

1. Run greedy decoding without a KV connector and record token IDs.
2. Use a connector that promises a block-aligned synchronous load and rejects
   it before copying KV.
3. Compare clean-base and patched output against the no-connector baseline for
   sync, async, and async EAGLE3 scheduling.
4. Repeat with real `LMCacheConnectorV1`, injecting a one-shot failure in a
   16-token retrieval before KV is copied.

## Test Result

- Focused tests: **16 passed**.
- Ruff check and format: **passed** for all five changed files.
- `git diff --check`: **passed**.
- Rebased cleanly onto `main` at `fe76112ff2`; focused tests and static checks
  were rerun after the final rebase.

Single-GPU negative control (NVIDIA RTX 5060 Ti, Model Runner V2 asserted,
greedy token-ID comparison):

| Configuration | Clean base | Patched |
|---|---:|---:|
| Controlled rejection, sync | differs from baseline | exact, 2/2 |
| Controlled rejection, async | differs from baseline | exact, 2/2 |
| EAGLE3 async, 2 draft tokens | differs from baseline | exact, 2/2 |
| Real LMCache rejection, sync | differs from scratch | exact |
| Real LMCache rejection, async | differs from scratch | exact |

The sync, async, EAGLE3, and real-LMCache async smoke cases were rerun after the
preceding main rebase and remained exact. The final intervening upstream commit
only changes ROCm/DeepSeek files; the five files in this PR were unchanged.

Not covered: multi-GPU pipeline parallelism, hybrid KV cache manager, layerwise
LMCache loading, or multi-request shared-block recovery. A separate ordinary
LMCache-hit fused-layout corruption observed on this stack is outside this
change's scope; the forced-failure test rejects before any cached KV copy.

AI assistance disclosure: OpenAI Codex assisted with the investigation,
implementation, and test orchestration. The human submitter reviewed all five
changed files, understands the change, and accepts maintenance responsibility.
